channel.description: Latest articles from Paste Media Group (pastemagazine.com)

item.title: The lost art of the mashup
item.description: Cultural Reset: YouTube megamixes were the last, gaudy flourish of a long mashup tradition, and their asphyxiation by copyright bots, slow‑core streaming, and social atomization doubles as an obituary for monoculture.

item.title: Refreshingly mature genre exercise Crime 101 is more than a cops-and-robbers intro course
item.description: Bart Layton's evocative take on the prestige and star-studded crime saga, Crime 101 has an unexpected polite streak.

item.title: On Clearly Cursed, PONY’s crunch-pop is full of messy coming-of-age charm
item.description: The Toronto duo bring their fuzzed-out guitars and dreamy vocals to grapple with toxic friendships, dead pets, and self-blame on their third album.

item.title: Slasher anti-franchise The Strangers remains unknowable five films later
item.description: Renny Harlin's remake trilogy complicates the dour simplicity of The Strangers with additional genre anonymity.

item.title: Conservative lawmakers plan to investigate Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl halftime show
item.description: Cranky representatives Andy Ogles and Mark Alford are leading a charge against the NFL and NBC, citing Bunny’s performance for “explicit displays” and “glorifying unspeakable depravities.”

item.title: R.I.P. James Van Der Beek, star of Dawson's Creek
item.description: The actor had previously shared his colorectal cancer diagnosis in 2024.

item.title: John C. Reilly wants you to dream a little dream of Mister Romantic before Valentine’s Day
item.description: Before his sold-out holiday show at Glendale Presbyterian Church, Reilly is getting into the sentimental spirit with two new singles.

item.title: R.I.P. Bud Cort, Harold And Maude star
item.description: Just 22 when cast in the Hal Ashby cult classic, Cort had a long career that stretched well into the 2010s.
